Troubleshooting ​

Every message below is a real string Saidi emits, grouped by where the failure comes from. Each entry is the symptom you see, what caused it, and what to do. The orchestrator almost never fails silently — the few places where it does are called out explicitly.

Runs & plans ​

Plan rejected: followed by a bulleted list

set_plan validates the whole plan before freezing it, and rejects the lot rather than accepting a half-usable checklist. The bullets are the actual problems:

BulletMeaning
The plan has no tasks.Empty items array
Task <label> has no acceptanceCriteria. Every task needs at least one.A task nothing can verify
Task <label> has no OBSERVABLE acceptance criterion …Every criterion is an opinion, not a file/command/count/output
Task <label> has an unrunnable check …The check command was refused (see below)
Task <label>: <kind> must name one acceptance criterion exactly.A proof's criterion doesn't match any criterion text
Task <label>: fileExists proof needs a safe relative path.Absolute, ~, or escaping path
Task <label>: assetCount proof needs minCount >= 1.Missing or zero minCount
Task <label>: check … must set \criterion` to the EXACT text …`A check that certifies nothing

Fix: re-plan with concrete criteria. Criterion matching is normalised for case, whitespace and trailing punctuation only — the words themselves must match. See Plans & Tasks.

A check is called "unrunnable"

Checks are model-authored and executed as real shell commands with no tool gate, so they are validated at plan time. The reasons are exact: the check is empty; command substitution ($(…), backticks, ${…}) is not allowed in a check; a check may not write output to a file; sed may not edit files in place in a check.

Fix: a check reads and exits with a status. If you need something written first, that is work for a task, not for its check.

Amendment rejected: followed by bullets

amend_plan refuses amendments that would rewrite history:

  • Task "<id>" is already done and cannot be dropped from the plan.
  • Task "<id>" would lose its acceptance criteria. Criteria may be corrected, never removed …
  • Task "<id>" is done; an amendment cannot reopen it. Add a NEW task for the follow-up work.

Fix: add a new task for the follow-up instead of reopening the old one.

There is no plan to amend yet — call set_plan first. — amend_plan before any plan exists.

Not finishing: …

Two separate gates on finish_run, both listing the offending steps. N plan steps are still open — complete them, or amend_plan with a reason. N steps completed without passing verification — verification is on and a task is marked done without a passing TaskVerification; re-delegate so its acceptance criteria are actually checked.

The run was stopped. — the run's abort signal fired mid-tool: you pressed stop, or the run was cancelled while a delegation was in flight. Returned from every long-running run tool. Resume or reopen the run. This run no longer exists. — the run record was deleted between the tool call and its execution.

A verifier verdict you can't parse

Four strings, four different things: Verifier returned no clear verdict: … (replied, but not in the expected form — failureKind: proof_missing); Verifier could not complete: … (the verifier agent errored — environment_failure); Verification could not run: … (the harness threw before reaching a verifier); No acceptance criteria to check against. (verdict skipped, which is not a pass).

The run escalates instead of retrying

The reconciler stops the dispatch loop and hands back to you with one of: the run has no plan; a full dispatch pass changed nothing — the work is not progressing; N tasks are blocked; N tasks used every attempt; N task cannot start (dependencies never completed); the plan cannot progress. Parts are joined with and. The second is a stall guard — two consecutive dispatch passes produced an identical progress signature. Amend the plan or steer manually.

Hit a transient network error (…). Any committed work and attachments survived; auto-resuming shortly.

A retryable provider/network error inside the run loop, within the auto-resume budget. Nothing to do — committed work and attachments are intact.

Delegation ​

The target or the task id doesn't resolve

  • No agent or project matches "<target>". Known: … — registry names are exact, not fuzzy. Use one of the listed names.
  • "<target>" is ambiguous — it matches projects: … Delegate again with the exact registry name. — the target prefix-matched more than one project.
  • Unknown checklist taskId "<id>". Set the plan first. — the id isn't in the frozen plan.
  • Task "<id>" is not ready; dependencies still open: … — dependsOn is enforced by the engine, not by the model's judgement. Finish the dependencies, or amend the plan.

delegate_batch refusals

MessageCause
delegate_batch requires a distinct taskId for every item.Two items claim the same task
Unknown checklist taskId(s): … They must exist in the plan.Ids not in the plan
Not batching: dependencies are still open for …At least one item isn't ready
delegate_batch requires distinct agents/projects. Work aimed at the same target must be sequenced with delegate.Two items target the same agent
Approval-gated work cannot start in a batch: … Delegate those tasks individually.A target is on approval: confirm

The last one is deliberate: an approval gate needs a human decision per change, which a batch cannot express. See Delegation.

A guard message that tells the model to stop repeating itself

Three run-scoped counters, three messages:

  • Repetition — That exact task has already been given to "<target>" 3 times in this run and repeating it will not change the result. Fingerprint is case- and whitespace-normalised, so rephrasing does not reset it.
  • Attempts — This checklist task has used all 3 of its attempts. Do NOT retry it again …
  • Consecutive failure — "<target>" has already failed 3 times in a row on this run — do NOT delegate the same work to it again.

These come back as non-error results on purpose: an isError result is exactly what provokes another retry. Defaults are 3/3/3 and are operator-configurable; an operator message to the run clears all three counters.

This has already failed 3 times against the same target in this turn. … — an agent-level guard: three consecutive failures of the same tool against the same target within one call. In-memory, per call. The tool call is wrong, not flaky.

This agent is in read-only (ask) mode. / The tool "<name>" is not in this agent's permitted tools (Settings → Permissions).

The agent tried a write-class tool in ask mode, or a tool outside its allowlist. Fix: delegate in work mode, or widen the agent's permitted tools. See Approval & Spend Guardrails.

Your workspace admin hasn't granted you the "<agent>" agent — ask an admin to allow it, or use a different agent.

The run creator's agent access governs every delegation in the run, including ones a lead routes. Fix: have an admin grant the agent, or route to a different one.

A delegation parks as a pending approval

You see This change to <project> needs your approval before I proceed: and the run goes to awaiting_input — the project is on approval: confirm. Approve or Deny in the Runs tab or from the main chat; the run applies the change itself once you approve. If you deny, the task is set to blocked with evidence Approval denied: <note>. A lead that hits the same gate reports back instead (<agent> is on approval:confirm — a change there needs Said's explicit approval, which I can't grant from inside a lead delegation.), because a lead cannot grant your approval.

A file read or a kill is refused

Two agent-level guards. A whole-file read above 256 KB with no offset/limit returns <file> is N MB — reading it whole floods your context window. Read a slice (offset/limit) or grep/sed -n for exactly what you need. A broad process-killing command returns a message ending To stop a server, kill only a PID this run started after verifying its cwd is inside the target repo. — and wrappers like timeout, env, sudo, nohup are unwrapped first, so hiding the command inside one does not help.

Git & branches ​

⚠️ <project> has uncommitted changes. Commit or stash them first, then ask me again.

Project work on a shared checkout found a dirty tree. Saidi will not clobber edits it did not make. One exception: a run resuming its own branch after a crash continues on top of its own interrupted work, with the status resuming over interrupted uncommitted work.

Fix: commit or stash, or let the run use a worktree.

<project> has uncommitted changes — switching branches now could lose them. Let the current work finish (or clean the tree) first. — you asked to switch the run's working branch while the tree is dirty.

"<branch>" is not a local branch of <project>. — the switch names a branch that doesn't exist locally. Remote-only branches are not resolved here.

git switch failed: <last line of git output> — raw git failure, last line only. Unknown project "<name>." / Unknown run. — the branch-switch target does not resolve.

worktree unavailable (<first line of git output>) — using the shared tree

Status line, not an error: the run tried to cut a private worktree and git refused, so it fell back to the shared checkout. The common cause is the same branch already checked out elsewhere (fatal: 'saidi/run-x' is already checked out at …), or the target directory not being a git repo at all. Fix: git worktree prune, or free the branch.

A git step hangs then fails

Git runs with explicit timeouts: 15s for reads, 120s for fetch origin --prune, 180s for worktree add, 60–120s for worktree remove/prune; evidence collection uses 15s and a 4 MB buffer. A slow or credential-prompting remote is the usual cause — Saidi never answers a credential prompt.

Work landed on a base branch you didn't expect

Base resolution walks staging, develop, main, master (each also tried as origin/<name>), plus any hint. In a worktree the base is what the worktree was cut from, recorded at creation — HEAD is never read back.

Agents & MCP ​

No response within 10s.

The MCP probe raced connect + listTools against a 10s timeout and lost. Fix: for stdio servers, run the command by hand; for HTTP servers, check the URL is reachable from the host running Saidi.

Authentication required — sign in to use this server.

The probe hit a 401 / UnauthorizedError / an invalid_token response, and flags needsAuth. A silently failed token refresh also lands here — the stale token is kept deliberately so the server 401s and the tab shows this rather than a refresh error. Fix: authorise from an interactive session; a headless or scheduled run cannot run an OAuth flow.

Not runnable — needs a `command` or a `url`. — the entry has neither a stdio command nor a URL. Unreachable. — the default when no transport ever produced a message; for a URL server, both StreamableHTTP and the SSE fallback failed. Any other transport error, including a malformed URL, is passed through verbatim.

MCP OAuth failures

MessageCause
Only http/sse MCP servers authenticate via OAuth.Auth started on a stdio server
The server did not produce an authorization URL.Provider never issued a redirect
Unknown or expired authorization request — restart from the MCP tab.Callback state not pending: server restarted, or more than 10 minutes elapsed
Authorization did not complete.Code exchange returned a non-authorised status
No authorization in progress — restart from the MCP tab.PKCE verifier missing

Tokens live at agents/<agent>/mcp-auth/<server>.json, written atomically. The callback is http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/mcp/oauth/callback — if you reach Saidi on a different host or port than it resolved for itself, the callback will not come back.

MCP registration is rejected

MCP server names must be 2–40 characters.; Use lowercase letters, digits, dashes, and underscores (must start with a letter or digit).; "<name>" is reserved for Saidi's built-in servers. (saidi, saidi_mem, saidi_dev); An MCP server needs a `command` (stdio) or a `url` (http/sse).; Failed to write mcp.json.; No MCP server "<name>" on this agent.

An MCP server disappears with no message at all

This is the one place worth knowing about: a malformed agents/<agent>/mcp.json, a missing or non-object mcpServers key, or an individual entry whose name fails validation is dropped silently. Fix: validate the file as JSON, check the key is mcpServers, and check every server name is already lowercase.

A call retries, or conspicuously doesn't

Three attempts total (initial plus two retries), exponential backoff from 500 ms capped at 8 s with full jitter. Retried: connection refused/reset/aborted, DNS failures, socket hang up, fetch failures, timeouts, overloaded, and HTTP 408/429/500/502/503/504/529. Never retried, and this wins over any of the above: 400/401/403, unauthorized, forbidden, and budget/turn-limit exhaustion. A retry only happens if nothing has been yielded yet — a stream that drops mid-response is re-thrown unchanged rather than replayed, since replaying would double-fire callbacks and duplicate the transcript.

Provider authentication failed. Check Settings → AI Providers, then retry. / The provider is rate-limited or overloaded — try again in a moment. / This turn hit its cost limit and stopped. / This turn hit its step limit and stopped.

Classified provider errors surfaced on a turn. The last two are your own configured per-turn budget and step ceilings, not provider errors.

Credits & limits ​

Insufficient credits: the wallet balance is $X. Ask your workspace owner to add credits to continue.

Cloud mode only, wallet at or below zero. The run is paused and the reason is appended to the thread as a SYSTEM event. Over HTTP this is the only 402 Saidi returns. The sibling message Your monthly usage budget ($X) is used up — it resets next month, or an admin can raise it. means member period spend has reached budget plus grant.

Mid-run pauses

  • Run paused: its cost reached the per-run ceiling of $X (runCostAlertUsd). Raise the ceiling in Settings, then resume the run.
  • Run paused: its cost reached your per-run cap of $X. An admin can raise the cap, then resume the run.
  • Run paused: its owner is no longer a member of this workspace — an admin can remove or reassign it.

The run is paused, not failed — raise the limit and resume. See Settings.

Usage checks are temporarily unavailable — please retry in a moment.

The membership/billing read threw. Enforcement fails closed, so work stops rather than running unmetered.

Access denials

You are no longer a member of this workspace.; This workspace is suspended — contact support.; This workspace no longer exists.; Run #<id> belongs to another member — you don't have access to it.; You don't have permission to <action> in this workspace — ask an admin. All checked before a run starts or an action runs.

Credits routes

Platform credits are available in cloud mode only. (404); Platform usage is available in cloud mode only. (404); You do not have permission to view workspace usage. (403 — needs billing.view or usage.viewOrg); MongoDB is required to load credits (credits are never served from memory).

Channels ​

Telegram: Invalid bot token (Telegram rejected it with 401).

Telegram rejected getMe. Re-copy the token from BotFather; saving it through the settings route validates it up front and returns Telegram rejected this token (401). Double-check you copied it from BotFather.

Telegram: Another process is polling this bot token (409).

Two Saidi instances (or another bot process) share one token. The poller logs [telegram] 409 — another poller holds this token; retrying… and keeps trying. Run one poller per token.

Telegram is simply off, with no error shown

A missing or empty bot token tears the channel down cleanly and clears the error field, so the status reads "not enabled" rather than "failed". The legacy env seed is TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN; live config lives in the channel-config store.

Telegram: ⛔ Not authorized. with your user id

The sender's Telegram user id isn't on the allow-list; the message includes the id so you can paste it into Settings → Telegram. Sent once per user id. A callback query from a non-allowed user gets the shorter Not authorized.

⚠ channel "<id>" failed to start: — the channel adapter threw during startup; the underlying error follows.

Webhooks return 4xx

generic webhook not configured (SAIDI_WEBHOOK_GENERIC_TOKEN); github webhook not configured (SAIDI_WEBHOOK_GITHUB_SECRET); stripe webhook not configured (SAIDI_WEBHOOK_STRIPE_SECRET); meta webhook not configured (SAIDI_WEBHOOK_META_SECRET); invalid token; invalid signature; malformed Stripe-Signature; stale or future Stripe timestamp (replay protection); unknown scheme "<x>" for <source> (use bearer | hmac | none).

Every one names the env var it wants. Set it and restart.

Mail is never delivered

⚠ SAIDI_MAIL_DRIVER=resend but SAIDI_RESEND_API_KEY is unset — mail dropped — the driver is set but the key isn't, so mail is dropped rather than queued. Send failures log ⚠ mail send failed (<status>):. Defaults: driver console, from Saidi <noreply@localhost>.

MongoDB is required to persist channel configuration (and the matching load / identity variants) — channel config and identities are Mongo-backed with no file fallback.

Where to look when something went wrong ​

Everything a Run did is readable from the console — you do not need shell access, and there is no server for you to log into.

QuestionWhere to look
What did the agents actually do?The Run thread — every delegation, tool call, cost and verdict, in order
Why did a task fail its gate?The verification log on the Run, which is append-only and survives plan amendments
What did this cost, and where?The Run's usage ledger, and Settings → Costs & Limits for the workspace total
What files did it produce?The Run's Files tab, backed by GET /api/runs/:id/files?path=
What is it doing right now?The live WebSocket feed behind the Run screen (run_event / run_update)

The Run thread is not exposed as a separate HTTP event stream — read it from GET /api/runs/:id, whose record includes thread.

Run tool semantics — what each tool refuses and why — are documented in Run Tools.
